text:
**Findings**

1. [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:74) high: `upsert_jobs` treats rows as unchanged using only `state`, `end`, and `elapsed_sec`, so corrected CPU/GPU/user/exit-code data is silently ignored.
2. [jobwatch/reports.py](/work/jobwatch/reports.py:14) medium: timestamp filtering and `MAX()` use lexicographic SQLite text comparisons, which are wrong when accepted ISO datetimes include timezone offsets.
3. [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:13) medium: schema creation has no migration/versioning path, so existing databases from older versions can remain incompatible while `connect()` appears successful.
4. [jobwatch/parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:137) medium: parsed rows accept empty users/partitions and negative CPU/GPU counts, allowing bad accounting data into reports.
5. [jobwatch/cli.py](/work/jobwatch/cli.py:121) low: report commands call `db.connect()`, which creates a brand-new empty database on typo/missing path instead of failing clearly.
6. [jobwatch/parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:73) low: `is_step()` classifies any `JobID` containing `.` as a step, which is brittle for non-basic Slurm job ID formats.
7. [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:13) low: the schema has no report-oriented indexes, so usage/failure/top reports will full-scan as the jobs table grows.

Overall, this is clean, readable small-package code with solid fixture coverage, but I would not approve it as-is for a production cleanup PR because of the silent stale-update bug and datetime correctness issue. Tests pass: `61 passed`; `compileall` could not complete because the workspace is read-only for `__pycache__` creation.

issues.description: Upsert unchanged detection ignores corrected resource/user/exit-code fields, silently preserving stale accounting data.
Report time filtering and newest-time selection compare ISO timestamp strings lexicographically, producing wrong results with timezone offsets.
Database initialization has no schema versioning or migrations, so older databases can remain structurally incompatible.
Row parsing accepts empty users/partitions and negative CPU/GPU counts, allowing invalid accounting data into reports.
Report commands create a missing database path and return empty reports, hiding typo or deployment-path mistakes.
Step detection treats any JobID containing a dot as a step, which can drop valid non-basic Slurm job identifiers.
Jobs table has no indexes for reference-time, state, user, or partition report queries, causing full scans as data grows.
